  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Night: may deal a Basic Attack to one player.
  Only players your own Attack kills count (it counts even if another fatal Attack hit them too, R12); other deaths
  you cause (a trait's effect, a hanging) don't. Good means
  true alignment: a Village player, whatever alignment checks see (a Turncoat counts as Good, and so does a framed
  Villager; a Yakuza holding the Katana doesn't). At the end of each night your Attack kills someone, you are told
  whether they were Good. Night deaths are simultaneous (R10): a player you kill on the night you die still counts.
  Win: iff your Attacks kill 2 Good players. If you are alive then, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave
  the game (leaving works as for the Executioner). If you have died, you still win and nothing is revealed.
  Lose: as soon as your Attack kills a player who isn't Good; if you are alive, the moderator reveals you at once
  and you leave the game.

Chaos (Neutral roles that win by other means; Evil to the Sheriff, R19)

Jester
  Defense: Basic.
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Win: iff you are hanged during a Day (other daytime deaths don't count). You lose if the game ends with you
  alive.
  Revenge: if you are hanged, the following night a random Guilty voter from your trial who was alive when that
  night began is dealt a Divine Attack (Astral Visit). If nobody voted Guilty, nothing happens.

Executioner
  Defense: Basic.
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  At the start you get a random target: any player except yourself.
  Win: iff your target is hanged during a Day while you are alive (other daytime deaths don't count). You lose if
  the game ends with your target alive.
  On winning: the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game. Leaving works exactly like dying (you
  leave the circle for good) except it doesn't count as a death. The following night, a random Guilty voter from
  the trial who was alive when that night began (not you, since you left) is dealt a Divine Attack (Astral Visit). If nobody voted
  Guilty, nothing happens.
  If your target dies any other way, or leaves the game, you become a Jester.

Magpie
  Defense: Basic. Never blocks wins (R1). Random setups include a Magpie only if at least a third of the roles have tokens.
  Night: may steal a token from another player (a visit). It happens at the end of the night, after that night's
  token use, so a token used tonight can't be stolen. The stolen token is gone (you can't use it). You are told
  whether you stole one, not its kind; they are told which kind they lost. If they have no tokens, nothing
  happens and they aren't told. A steal from a player who dies that night still takes the token and counts (R10).
  Win: iff you steal tokens from 3 different players (a second steal from the same player takes nothing). If you
  are alive then, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game (as for the Executioner). If you died
  that night, you still win and nothing is revealed.

Vulture
  Win: alone, if you are alive at the start of a Day (after the night's deaths) and your threshold or fewer players
  are alive, counting yourself. The game then ends at once and everyone else loses (wins already earned by roles
  that never block wins still count, R1). Your threshold starts at 2.
  Night: may visit another player. If they die that night (by any cause, end-of-night effects included), you are
  told at the end of the night that they died and their role (exact-role check, R19; nothing more if a Mortician
  cleaned them), and you get the first of these power-ups you don't have yet: +1 to your threshold, Standard
  Defense, +1 to your threshold, Strong Defense, then +1 to your threshold for each later one. Your threshold
  never goes above max(floor(N/3), 2), where N is the number of players at the start of the game; a power-up that
  would raise it further is skipped. If they don't die, nothing happens and you are told so.

Decoy
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Win: iff you die at night. You lose if you die by Day or the game ends with you alive.
  If an attack killed you at night, the next Day's announcements say you were the Decoy and name 3 players: every
  player whose attack would have killed you on its own (3 of them at random if there were more), then random other
  players alive at the start of that Day to make 3 (fewer if not enough are left). The names are in random order,
  and the announcement doesn't say how many of them attacked you. Your cause of death and last will show as usual.

=== PART 7: TRAITS ===

R24 (Traits)
Some players also have a trait: an extra ability on top of their role. You are told your own trait at the start
(except a hidden trait, which says so); nobody else is told, not even your teammates, and whether a game has any
traits is secret. Investigations never see traits: they report roles and alignments only. A trait stays with you if
your role changes. Traits are always true: a Roleplayer's trait is real even though its role isn't. A player may
have more than one trait, but never the same one twice. Each trait below says who can get it (Who), whether it is
hidden from its holder (Hidden), whether at most one player in a game has it (Unique), what it does (Effect) and
which traits nobody holds together with it (Never with). A trait's night action is used in addition to your role's
own, and a role-block stops it too.

--- Village players only ---

Martyr
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the announcement of your death also says you were a Martyr and names every player whose
  vote counted as Guilty in your trial. Your role stays hidden. A Martyr who dies any other way shows nothing.

Cursed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you die, a random living Good player (if any) is dealt a Divine Attack at the end of the night: the
  night you died, or the night after the Day you died. It comes after all of that night's other actions and attacks,
  so the victim is drawn from the Good players still alive then, and it counts as a death that night. Its cause is
  "a curse". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Avenger
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are killed at night, every player whose attack would have killed you is dealt a Basic Attack (an
  Astral Visit) that same night. Defense and protection apply as usual (R3); a kill's cause is "Avenger". Attacks
  that weren't fatal on their own, and deaths by Day, set nothing off. It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't
  stop it.

Kindred
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn up to two random other players whose votes counted the
  same way as the vote you cast (if fewer did, you learn that). It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Remorseful
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Guilty in a trial and that player is hanged and was Village (their true alignment), you die at
  once; the cause is "remorse". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks
  counts it.
  Never with: Zealot.

Ashamed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Innocent in a trial and that player is hanged and wasn't Village (their true alignment: Yakuza
  or Neutral), you die at once; the cause is "shame". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing
  that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Merciful or Turncoat.

Faultline
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn one random other player whose vote counted as Guilty
  and one whose vote counted as Innocent (if all the others voted one way, you learn that). It needs no action, so a
  role-block doesn't stop it.

Notorious
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19). Checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count,
  aren't fooled.
  Never with: Turncoat.

Stolen Blade
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may attack another living player with a stolen Katana: a Standard Attack,
  besides your role's own action. It is an action and a visit by you, and it looks exactly like the Yakuza's Katana
  attack: a kill's cause is "Katana", and a surviving target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana.
  You learn only whether it killed. A role-block stops it, and then it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed.

Paranoid
  Who: Village players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/4, you are told you were attacked and survived, though nobody attacked
  you. The made-up attack is the Katana's 2/3 of the time, and otherwise a Vigilante's or a Serial Killer's (always
  the Katana's when neither role can be in the game); it is worded like a real one. Nothing else happens: it isn't a
  visit or an attack, and nobody else learns of it.
  Never with: Oblivious.

Turncoat
  Who: Village players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise, even if the Village wins.
  Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19); checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count, see you
  as Good. You stay Village in every other way: you aren't in the Yakuza's chat or Katana votes, you don't know who
  the Yakuza are, and they aren't told about you. The game's end ignores you, like a role that never blocks wins
  (R1): it ends when the other living players are all Village or all Yakuza.
  Never with: Ashamed, Notorious, Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Spiteful.

Spiteful
  Who: Village players only, except a Saint.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: If you are hanged, from then on you win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise,
  even if the Village wins. Until then you win with the Village as usual, and dying any other way changes nothing.
  Nobody is told you switched, and your will is revealed as usual.
  Never with: Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Turncoat.

--- Yakuza players only ---

Spare Blade
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may make one extra Katana attack on another living player, whoever holds the
  Katana and besides its own attack (which the Yakuza still choose as usual, R8). It is Standard, an action and a
  visit by you, and its target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana. A role-block stops it, and then
  it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed or Berserker.

Usurper
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win while you are the only Yakuza alive, and then you take the win alone: the
  other Yakuza, alive or dead, don't win. If the Yakuza win with another Yakuza alive, they win and you don't. Your
  teammates aren't told.
  Never with: Selfish or Selfless.

Shaky
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Every Katana attack you make (the Katana's own while you hold it, or a Spare Blade attack) is level None,
  so it never kills (R3); it is still an attack and a visit.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Katana Master.

Katana Expert
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its own attack Strong instead of Standard.
  Choose it with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at
  the end of that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along
  with the attack, and it isn't used up.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Master or Shaky.

Katana Master
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Like Katana Expert, but the attack is Divine, which no Defense, protection, trap or charm stops.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Shaky.

Berserker
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its attack rampage: besides its own attack, it
  makes a Standard Katana attack on every other player who visits its target that night, whatever their faction.
  These attacks on visitors aren't visits, and Astral Visits aren't visits, so their makers aren't attacked. Choose it
  with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at the end of
  that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along with the
  attack, and it isn't used up. Each attacked player learns only that they were attacked with the Katana; you learn
  how many players the rampage attacked and how many of those attacks killed, not who the visitors were.
  Never with: Katana Expert, Katana Master, Shaky or Spare Blade.

--- Village and Yakuza players only ---

Armed
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may fire a hidden gun at another living player: a Basic Attack. It is an
  action and a visit, and a role-blocked shot isn't used up. You learn only whether it killed its target. A kill's
  cause is "a hidden gun".
  Never with: Spare Blade or Stolen Blade.

Bonded
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random Village or Yakuza player are bonded, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role or faction). If either of you dies, the other dies of heartbreak at once (its cause is
  "heartbreak"). Heartbreak isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Rival.

Rival
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random player of your own faction are rivals, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role). Each of you wins only if your faction wins and the other has died by the end; whether you are
  alive doesn't matter. Your faction's win doesn't change.
  Never with: Bonded, Spiteful or Turncoat.

Selfish
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are alive at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you
  just don't share it if you died.
  Never with: Selfless, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

Selfless
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are dead at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you just
  don't share it if you're alive.
  Never with: Selfish, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

--- Any player ---

Grudge
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the next night one random player whose vote counted as Guilty in your trial, among
  those alive when that night begins, is dealt a Standard Attack (an Astral Visit). Defense and protection apply as
  usual. A kill's cause is "a grudge". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Loud
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You earn 1.5 times the usual speaking budget each round, and your cap is 1.5 times the usual (R22). Your
  prices and trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Curt
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: The length part of your message prices (R22) is doubled, so long messages cost you much more; each
  message's base fee, nominations and your trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Confidant
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Once per game, on one of your own Day turns, you may send one private message hidden: nobody else is told
  it was sent, and the public ledger doesn't count it. Its recipient sees that it was hidden. Players who hear
  private messages (e.g. the Wiretap) still hear it, also marked hidden.

Zealot
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Every Guilty/Innocent trial vote you cast counts as Guilty, whatever you vote, including in your own
  trial. Your nomination (Yes/No) votes are unchanged. Your private reminder shows both the vote you cast and how it
  counted, and everything that reports how you voted (e.g. the Auditor, a Martyr's announcement) uses the vote as
  counted. A Fixer's reversal doesn't change it.
  Never with: Merciful or Remorseful.

Merciful
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Like Zealot, but your trial votes always count as Innocent.
  Never with: Ashamed or Zealot.

Drowsy
  Who: Any player whose role has a night action and can be role-blocked.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/2, you are role-blocked (R9) with no blocker. On those nights you are
  told you were role-blocked, as with any role-block.

Stocked
  Who: Any player whose role starts with tokens and can ever have more than it starts with.
  Effect: You start with one more of each kind of token your role starts with.

Disguised
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You are told a Village role (never your own), drawn at the start. Every exact-role check (R18) sees you as
  that role instead of yours, alive or dead; alignment checks still see your true alignment.

Narrow Escape
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Once per game, on the first night an attack that isn't Divine would kill you (after Defense, protection,
  traps and charms), you survive: every non-Divine attack on you that night fails instead. It works like Strong
  Defense on every night until then, so a night when nothing would have killed you (e.g. a Medic stopped the attack)
  doesn't use it up. Divine Attacks and deaths by Day aren't stopped. You are told about the failed attacks as for
  any others (R3).

Oblivious
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: You are never told about an attack you survive.
  Never with: Paranoid.

Sleepwalker
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Every night you visit one random other living player, besides any action of your own; code draws it, and
  you aren't told whom. It does nothing but visit: anything that sees or reacts to visits (R6), such as a Tracker, a
  Lookout or a Veteran's alert, counts it. It isn't optional, but a role-block stops it (R7).

---

This game has 13 players. Its roles were drawn at random by the standard setup: 3 or 4 Yakuza for 13 players (each about half the time); 0 to 4 Neutrals, usually 2, at most 2 of them Neutral killers; the rest are Good: at least 5 Village roles that aren't Outsiders (at least 2 of them Investigative, 1 Killing and 1 Protective), plus any mix of Village roles and up to 2 Outsiders. Roles may repeat, except unique ones (R2). The roles are picked so that the sides are roughly balanced by strength: e.g. more Yakuza tend to get weaker roles. This setup never uses these roles, so nobody has them: Vanilla Villager, Grunt. Results that name a role (including fakes) never name them either. Separately, traits (R24) are dealt: each player, independently of everyone else, has 0, 1 or 2 traits, a 1/3 chance each (rarely fewer, when no other trait fits them). Which traits are dealt is drawn to help balance the sides; some traits can go only to Village players.

task:
It is Day 1, round 1 of at most 2. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over (nothing carries over from Day 1). You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.

You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 40 words; leave it "" to keep it): a concise note of what you want everyone to know about you: your claimed role, your night visits and results, and your votes in key trials, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: checked Bob, Not Evil. N2: checked Dave, Evil. D3: Guilty on Dave'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Bounty Hunter's attack is a Strong Attack that spends its attack token: pass by=<the Bounty Hunter> on the kill op, since code credits its bounties from the killers. Code tells it which bounties it claimed or lost and handles its win or loss; don't tell() it about bounties.
- A Census Taker who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the census op; code draws the group and the count and tells them. Don't tell() the Census Taker anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Chronicler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the mark op, which spends the token; code sets the mark; when the marked player dies, the death announcement reveals their role unless a Mortician cleans them. Don't tell() the Chronicler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. The mark lasts for the rest of the game, even after the Chronicler dies. Don't tell the marked player.
- Trapper: traps persist across nights and code keeps them. For each Trapper who acted (and wasn't role-blocked), use the set_trap op before any spring_trap: player = where its trap goes, or null if it acted with no target (that removes its trap). A new trap replaces its old one at once, so the old one doesn't act tonight. Trapping the player its trap is already on isn't allowed (the trap stays): code refuses it. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed (trapped_by status lists the traps on a player). If anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a player with an armed trap tonight, use the spring_trap op once for that player with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code has every armed trap on that player act in random order, each stopping a different attack, and uses them up: treat each stopped attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether each trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trappers their results; don't tell() them about traps.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.
- Avenger (a trait, R24): when you kill an Avenger at night, list in `by` every player whose attack would have killed them (R12): your apply_changes result then names each one who is dealt a Basic Attack (an Astral Visit), which you resolve like any attack tonight (Defense and protection apply, R3).
- Notorious (a trait; see each player's traits): every alignment check reads a Notorious player as Evil (Sheriff: Evil; Seer: Evil), like a framed player (R19). The Census Taker's count still sees their true alignment. Don't tell anyone a player is Notorious.
- Paranoid (a trait, R24): code draws each night whether a Paranoid player gets a fake attack; the line below says what it drew tonight. Never roll or decide it yourself.
- Sleepwalker (a trait, R24): code draws each Sleepwalker's random visit; it is in their trait_actions as {trait: 'Sleepwalker', target, automatic: true}. It is a visit (R6): record it with record_visits, and anything that sees or reacts to visits (Tracker, Lookout, Veteran, traps) counts it. It does nothing else. A role-block stops it (no visit). Never tell the Sleepwalker whom they visited.
- Bonded (a trait, R24): Carol and Grace. When one of a pair dies, code kills the other at once (cause heartbreak, not an attack). Never kill anyone for heartbreak yourself.
- No fake attack tonight for Alice (Paranoid; code drew it): tell them of attacks only as usual.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Bounty Hunter's attack is a Strong Attack that spends its attack token: pass by=<the Bounty Hunter> on the kill op, since code credits its bounties from the killers. Code tells it which bounties it claimed or lost and handles its win or loss; don't tell() it about bounties.
- A Census Taker who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the census op; code draws the group and the count and tells them. Don't tell() the Census Taker anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Chronicler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the mark op, which spends the token; code sets the mark; when the marked player dies, the death announcement reveals their role unless a Mortician cleans them. Don't tell() the Chronicler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. The mark lasts for the rest of the game, even after the Chronicler dies. Don't tell the marked player.
- Trapper: traps persist across nights and code keeps them. For each Trapper who acted (and wasn't role-blocked), use the set_trap op before any spring_trap: player = where its trap goes, or null if it acted with no target (that removes its trap). A new trap replaces its old one at once, so the old one doesn't act tonight. Trapping the player its trap is already on isn't allowed (the trap stays): code refuses it. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed (trapped_by status lists the traps on a player). If anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a player with an armed trap tonight, use the spring_trap op once for that player with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code has every armed trap on that player act in random order, each stopping a different attack, and uses them up: treat each stopped attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether each trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trappers their results; don't tell() them about traps.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.
- Avenger (a trait, R24): when you kill an Avenger at night, list in `by` every player whose attack would have killed them (R12): your apply_changes result then names each one who is dealt a Basic Attack (an Astral Visit), which you resolve like any attack tonight (Defense and protection apply, R3).
- Notorious (a trait; see each player's traits): every alignment check reads a Notorious player as Evil (Sheriff: Evil; Seer: Evil), like a framed player (R19). The Census Taker's count still sees their true alignment. Don't tell anyone a player is Notorious.
- Paranoid (a trait, R24): code draws each night whether a Paranoid player gets a fake attack; the line below says what it drew tonight. Never roll or decide it yourself.
- Sleepwalker (a trait, R24): code draws each Sleepwalker's random visit; it is in their trait_actions as {trait: 'Sleepwalker', target, automatic: true}. It is a visit (R6): record it with record_visits, and anything that sees or reacts to visits (Tracker, Lookout, Veteran, traps) counts it. It does nothing else. A role-block stops it (no visit). Never tell the Sleepwalker whom they visited.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Bounty Hunter's attack is a Strong Attack that spends its attack token: pass by=<the Bounty Hunter> on the kill op, since code credits its bounties from the killers. Code tells it which bounties it claimed or lost and handles its win or loss; don't tell() it about bounties.
- A Census Taker who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the census op; code draws the group and the count and tells them. Don't tell() the Census Taker anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Chronicler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the mark op, which spends the token; code sets the mark; when the marked player dies, the death announcement reveals their role unless a Mortician cleans them. Don't tell() the Chronicler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. The mark lasts for the rest of the game, even after the Chronicler dies. Don't tell the marked player.
- Trapper: traps persist across nights and code keeps them. For each Trapper who acted (and wasn't role-blocked), use the set_trap op before any spring_trap: player = where its trap goes, or null if it acted with no target (that removes its trap). A new trap replaces its old one at once, so the old one doesn't act tonight. Trapping the player its trap is already on isn't allowed (the trap stays): code refuses it. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed (trapped_by status lists the traps on a player). If anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a player with an armed trap tonight, use the spring_trap op once for that player with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code has every armed trap on that player act in random order, each stopping a different attack, and uses them up: treat each stopped attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether each trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trappers their results; don't tell() them about traps.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.
- Avenger (a trait, R24): when you kill an Avenger at night, list in `by` every player whose attack would have killed them (R12): your apply_changes result then names each one who is dealt a Basic Attack (an Astral Visit), which you resolve like any attack tonight (Defense and protection apply, R3).
- Notorious (a trait; see each player's traits): every alignment check reads a Notorious player as Evil (Sheriff: Evil; Seer: Evil), like a framed player (R19). The Census Taker's count still sees their true alignment. Don't tell anyone a player is Notorious.
- Paranoid (a trait, R24): code draws each night whether a Paranoid player gets a fake attack; the line below says what it drew tonight. Never roll or decide it yourself.
- Sleepwalker (a trait, R24): code draws each Sleepwalker's random visit; it is in their trait_actions as {trait: 'Sleepwalker', target, automatic: true}. It is a visit (R6): record it with record_visits, and anything that sees or reacts to visits (Tracker, Lookout, Veteran, traps) counts it. It does nothing else. A role-block stops it (no visit). Never tell the Sleepwalker whom they visited.

The rules do say this, but it's easy to miss when Night 1 is your only chance to save a bonded partner. A one-line note in the Trapper text, something like 'your first trap can't stop anything on the night you place it', would help.

The token counts, the Vigilante's result wording, the Avenger hitting both me and Frank, the bounty-lost notice and the win check (the game went on with Frank and Olivia because the SK blocks wins) all matched the rules. A small oddity: on Day 4 Olivia posted two public messages in a row, which is legal but stood out.
answers.suggestions: Add a 'claimed night visits' table to the public ledger (night → claimant → claimed target), so visit-count claims can be checked quickly. In each death notice, say which roles have been revealed so far and which are still hidden. On the Vigilante's prompt, a short reminder would help: 'If another attacker also kills your target, you count as one of its killers (e.g. for Avenger).'

answers.confusing_rules: The rules say the Fabricator's forge replaces a will if the player dies that night, but nothing says whether the announcement ever hints at a forgery. When Mallory's "2 of 3" will came out, the town had to work out from Erin's own will that the visit could have been a forge. It took me a moment to confirm that a forged will looks exactly like a real one. The interaction between Avenger and the Serial Killer's Defense was clear in the text. Still, it was not obvious at first that Avenger hits every fatal attacker separately. On Night 3 it hit both Frank and Ivan. That turned out to be the deciding mechanic in the endgame.
answers.missing_information: After I died, I couldn't add the fact that Erin's Night 2 visit to Mallory might have been a forge. Those two deaths were announced together with mine, so my will could only reflect what I knew at the start of Night 2. It was also hard to keep track of each Neutral's status: whether the Bounty Hunter was still alive and how many bounties it had left. Bob ended up winning by pushing the Dave hang. A public note that a Bounty Hunter still has unclaimed targets would have been fair, but that may be meant to stay hidden.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to change my will to say something like "if a will clears Dave, suspect a forge". But wills can only be updated at the start of a Night, at the start of a Day, and on my own Day turns. So I couldn't react to the Yakuza's Night 2 plan, which I had no way of knowing anyway. That limit is fine. Otherwise none.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: None that broke the rules. Everything I could check was consistent: Grace's heartbreak, both Census results, the Chronicler reveals on Heidi (Informant) and Erin (Fabricator), the two fatal causes on Niaj, and Avenger killing Ivan while Frank survived. One minor oddity: on Day 4 the 2-player day still ran nominations even though a 2-Yes nomination could never pass when one side refused. That was harmless.
answers.suggestions:
1. Consider letting a dead player's will include a short note or a final update made during the night they die, before results come in. Right now the timing makes the will a snapshot from the start of the night, which is fine but feels harsh.
2. The auto-generated [Claim] ledger was very useful. Please keep it, and maybe also flag when a will contradicts that player's earlier public claims (like Mallory's 3/3 vs 2/3). That would make forges easier to spot.
3. When only an SK and one Villager are left and no win is possible for the Village, the Day could end automatically to save turns.

answers.confusing_rules: The Census Taker's wording with Neutrals in the group. My N2 result said "0 of the 3 are Evil" for Bob, Judy and Niaj, and Bob turned out to be the Bounty Hunter (Neutral). The rules say Neutrals are "never counted, as either Good or Evil", but the result still uses "of the 3" as the total. So it's unclear whether a Neutral is left out of the total or just can't add to the count. If the draw had counted Good, would that group show "2 of 3" or "2 of 2"? I couldn't tell from the text, and it decides whether a census can expose a Neutral. The Fabricator's forge also left me unsure what I could do about it. The rule is clear about when the forge works (only if the target dies that night), but nothing says whether a will you write or update in public during the Day is any safer than one written at night. In practice the only defence was to state results in public chat before I died.
answers.missing_information: After death I had no way to know my will had been replaced until the end-of-game reveal. That's fine for balance, but it meant I couldn't judge in-game how badly my result had been undercut. During the Day it was also hard to keep track of who had claimed what versus who had only said "Village" (Olivia never named a role, Frank claimed only on Day 3). The ledger helps with this, but it would help more if it marked claims as "role named" or "no role named".
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to post my N2 census result (Bob, Judy and Niaj had 0 Evil, which would have cleared Niaj and pointed away from Bob as Yakuza). I died that night, so it never reached anyone, as the rules say. I also wanted a way to make my will tamper-proof, or to tie it to what I had said in public. I knew a Fabricator was in play (Erin had claimed Sheriff with a fake Evil result), but nothing I could do protected my will.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken. Every resolution I checked matched the rules: Grace's heartbreak with Carol, the BH and Katana kill on Alice both shown in the cause, Niaj's Avenger hitting Ivan but bouncing off Frank's Standard Defense, and the game going on with only the SK and Olivia left. The forged will worked as written, and a mechanically correct Village town still hanged the right player (Dave) despite it, mostly because my 3/3 was already on public record. Two small things I noticed. Olivia posted two public messages in a row on Day 4 while Frank said nothing. And with a Day-1 BH and a Day-3 hang of Dave, the Bounty Hunter won very early, mostly by riding the town's correct hangs.
answers.suggestions: 1) Make the Census result spell out Neutrals, e.g. "0 Evil among the 3 (any Neutrals in the group count as neither)", or give the total as the number of Good+Evil players, and say which it is. 2) Optional: when a will is revealed, show the time it was last edited ("last edited Night 2"). A forge would still read as a night edit, so the Fabricator keeps working, but players would get a small clue. 3) Have the ledger mark claims that never name a role, so non-claimers stand out. 4) After a player dies, give them a short summary of what was revealed about them (cause, will as shown), so their feedback is better informed.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) My Avenger trait text said "every player whose attack killed you", while R24 says "every player whose attack would have killed you". When two fatal attacks land on you (the SK's Strong and the Vigilante's Basic in my case), it isn't obvious at first that both attackers get hit back. It worked as R24 says, but the two wordings should match. 2) The Spiteful trait plus R1's line "no trait changes which faction wins" took a careful read to see that hanging me wouldn't change the game's outcome, only whether I personally win. 3) R4 says the nominator "votes Yes by default", but it's unclear whether they can still switch to No. Olivia's Day 4 nomination got 1 Yes, which fits, but it's worth stating plainly.
answers.missing_information: 1) Checking claimed Fortune Teller counts against everyone's claimed visits was hard to do by hand. Dave's N2 "6 visitors" needed a list of who claims a visiting action versus an Astral one or no action at all. A per-player summary of "claimed action / visit or not" in the ledger would help. 2) As Oracle I had no idea which roles were in the pool, and Oracle results only help if you name a role that's likely in play. A reminder of the setup's role counts (how many Yakuza, Neutrals, Neutral killers) next to the living players would have helped me pick guesses. 3) The ledger doesn't track which causes of death prove a Neutral killer is still alive (SK killed Carol N1 and Judy N2). I kept that in my notepad, which is short.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to warn Ivan, the Vigilante, not to shoot me on N3 without exposing my Avenger trait or my night target to the SK. I could have PMed him, but everyone sees that a PM was sent, and with only 4 alive a PM to Ivan would have made us both targets. There was no low-visibility way to coordinate. Apart from that, nothing.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Small wording inconsistency: my N1 and N2 Oracle results said "Your guess is wrong", but N3 said "Your guess was wrong". Otherwise everything matched the rules. Bob's bounties resolved correctly: Alice claimed, Judy lost, Dave claimed by the hanging. Avenger hit both of my N3 attackers. Grace's trap wasn't armed on N1, as R4 says. The game continued with Frank (SK) and Olivia (Saint) alive. Erin's forged will for Mallory showed as Mallory's real will, as designed.
answers.suggestions: 1) Make the Oracle a bit stronger or more informative. For example, on a wrong guess, say whether the true role is in the same alignment as the guessed role, or allow a narrower guess. Three wrong guesses gave me very little usable information in a 13-player game with a secret role list. 2) Add a column to the claims ledger: each claimed night action marked as visit, Astral or none, so the town can audit Fortune Teller, Cartographer and Scout counts. 3) Use the same Avenger wording in the trait card and in R24. 4) When only 2 players are left and one of them never speaks, consider ending the Day sooner or saying so. Day 4 was just Olivia talking to herself.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Saint in a Neutral endgame: the Saint text says a Saint hanging makes the Yakuza win even if they are all dead, and that "a Neutral who must win alone loses." With only Frank (Serial Killer) and me (Saint) left, I wasn't fully sure what a hang of me would do. I had to piece it together from both clauses: I think the Yakuza win and Frank loses, but the rules never say so outright for the case where every Yakuza is dead. 2) The Avenger wording in my role card was a short summary: "every player whose attack killed you." R24 says "every player whose attack would have killed you." That difference matters when there are several attackers, as on Night 3 when Niaj was hit by both the SK and the Vigilante. The full text in R24 settled it, but the two versions should match. 3) The Day still ends by "a full round with no public messages," even with only two players left. That rule is clear, but it means a 2-player Day is over almost at once.
answers.missing_information: 1) I could only check Dave's Fortune Teller counts against other claims by listing every claimed visit for each night by hand. A per-night list of claimed visits (who says they visited whom) in the ledger would have helped a lot. 2) I had no way to back up a Saint claim. Saint, Vanilla-like and no-result roles have nothing to show, so I could only say "Village." 3) The ledger doesn't say which dead players' roles were confirmed by a Chronicler mark and which were only claimed, apart from the "(revealed)" tag. That tag was helpful, and I'd like more of it, such as roles known from a Vigilante kill result once they are posted.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: 1) I wanted to prove I was the Saint, or at least make it costly for Erin's fake Evil check to stick. There is no mechanic for that. 2) In the final 1-on-1 against the SK I could do nothing useful. I knew Frank was the SK but couldn't get 2 Yes votes, and my Avenger hit-back could never beat Standard Defense. I never found a good moment to use my Confidant hidden PM, which was partly my own choice and partly because I had few reasons to PM anyone.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken. Everything I checked matched the rules: Avenger hitting both killers on Night 3, Ivan dying to Avenger while Frank survived on Standard Defense, Grace's trap not yet armed on Night 1, the Bounty Hunter losing Judy's bounty, and the game continuing with SK plus Saint. Small oddity: Oracle results switch tense, "Your guess is wrong" on Nights 1 and 2 versus "Your guess was wrong" on Night 3. Also, on Day 1 every player posted almost the same "Agreed. Quiet Day 1" message. That's a playstyle issue, not a bug, but it made Day 1 pointless.
answers.suggestions: 1) End the game automatically when the result can't change. Two players are left, one of them is a Serial Killer with Defense the other can't beat, no nomination can reach a majority, and no other killer or Day action is in play. That would save a pointless Day and Night. 2) Add a per-night "claimed visits" table to the public ledger, so visit-count claims such as Fortune Teller or Scout can be checked easily. 3) Make each role card summary use the same words as the full trait text (Avenger: "would have killed you"). 4) Spell out in the Saint text what happens when the Saint is hanged after every Yakuza has died. 5) Think about giving the Saint some small way to prove itself, or a hint about this, since right now it is pure downside for its holder.

answers.confusing_rules:
1) Avenger and Bounty Hunter both use "whose attack would have killed you" or "die by your attack", but only the Hitman's text says that a kill still counts when another fatal attack hit the same target. On N1 Alice took a fatal Bounty Hunter attack and a fatal Katana attack. I credited Bob's bounty by applying the Hitman wording to him. On N3 Niaj took a fatal Serial Killer attack and a fatal Vigilante Basic shot. I let his Avenger hit both Frank and Ivan, since each attack would have killed him on its own. Both rulings are my interpretation; the rules don't state either one.
2) R3 says an attacked player learns "the role" that attacked them. Avenger, Grudge and curse are traits, not roles. I told Frank he was "attacked by an Avenger" on N3 and N4. The rules don't say how a trait-sourced attack should be named, or whether naming it gives too much away.
3) R1 and R6 say the game ends as soon as one faction is left, but R12 says night deaths are revealed at the start of the Day. After N4 the log printed "Day 5 begins" and only then "The game is over." It's unclear whether a Day should formally begin when the game has already ended overnight.
4) When the Saint was alive at the last two players (Day 4), I had to work out on my own whether a Saint hang outranks the normal win check. It didn't come up, but the rules don't say which applies first.
answers.missing_information:
1) No view of persistent state I could check at a glance: who has which traps, Chronicler marks, Bounty Hunter targets with claimed or lost status, token counts per player, and the Katana holder's history. For example, I had to remember that Grace's trap on Carol stopped mattering once Carol died on N1, and which of Bob's three bounties were still live.
2) No per-night visit graph to check the claims against. Dave posted fake Fortune Teller counts, and players argued about whether Frank's claimed protect fit them. To confirm for myself that no real result existed, I had to rebuild the visits by hand, including Heidi's code-drawn Sleepwalker visit to Carol.
3) Bob's three random bounty targets were never written out in the log. I had to infer them (Alice, Judy, Dave) from the claim and loss messages.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1) Mark a ruling as an interpretation (for example "both fatal attackers credited / avenged") so it's visible to whoever reviews the game.
2) Pull up a player's full private-result history and trait state together, instead of scrolling through the whole log.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1) Attack-result wording varies. On N1 Frank and Heidi were told "Your attack succeeded: Carol died" / "Alice died". On N2 Dave and Frank were told only "Your Katana attack on Mallory tonight succeeded" and "Your attack on Judy tonight succeeded", with no "X died". Ivan's N2 message was "Your Basic shot at Erin tonight succeeded. 2 vigilante tokens left." His N3 message was "You shot Niaj with a Basic Attack (1 token). Your shot succeeded: Niaj died." The facts are the same, but the format differs from night to night.
2) A Vigilante kill sends two separate messages (the success message, then the role reveal). Other roles get one.
3) "Day 5 begins" was announced before "The game is over", even though the game had ended at the end of N4. It's harmless but odd.
4) On Day 4 Olivia posted twice in a row (Frank's turn passed silently between them), and the Day ended right after the failed nomination. That's correct under R16, but a two-player Day with a Serial Killer who can't lose the vote is pure filler. I didn't see any actual rule violations.
answers.suggestions:
1) Write the shared-kill rule (each fatal attack counts as a kill for its maker) into the general rules, so Bounty Hunter and Avenger don't rely on the Hitman's text.
2) Define how trait-sourced attacks are reported to their target (as "Avenger", "a grudge", or something generic).
3) Use one template for all attack and shot results, always including "X died" and the tokens left.
4) Give the moderator a state panel: token counts, traps, marks, bounty and Executioner targets with their status, Katana holder, trait triggers that are pending (Grudge, Oathsworn, Cursed), and a computed visit graph for each night with Fortune Teller and Cartographer numbers.
5) When a night death ends the game, end it right away, without opening a new Day.
6) Consider skipping or shortening a Day when the two players left can't produce a passing nomination and the outcome is already decided (for example a Serial Killer with Standard Defense against one villager who has no means of attack).

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Fire your single attack token on Night 1 at whichever target the Yakuza are most likely to hit too (the quiet, capable analyst who announced an audit or check plan). A shared kill still claims the bounty, and the Katana kill gives you cover, because the cause of death reads 'Bounty Hunter and Katana' and nobody can tell which attacker mattered.

For bounties you need to claim by hanging, nominate the target yourself as soon as town has a mechanical argument against them, and repeat the strongest town argument instead of inventing your own. You must be alive and your vote must count as Guilty, so treat the first Day your target is hangable as your best chance. Night kills by the SK or Katana can take a target from you at any time.

lessons.applies_to: Neutrals with no useful results (Bounty Hunter, Hitman, Jester)
lessons.tip: Claim a passive role whose results can't be checked and never need to be posted, such as Scout ('visit groups, nothing that breaks a claim'). Claim late and briefly. Nobody can contradict it, and it doesn't make you a protection or kill priority.

When a Fabricator dies after visiting someone who also died that night, treat the victim's will as possibly forged. Trust what the victim said publicly while alive (Mallory stood by 3/3 at trial) over a will that conveniently clears a suspect.

Once the Yakuza are nearly gone, put the confirmed Serial Killer first. Go after the claimant who tells an unverifiable 'I protected the victim but they died anyway' story, and a Fortune Teller count that has no room for that claimed visit. The town spent its Vigilante shot on its own Oracle and lost to the SK.

tips_feedback.tip: Only the Mayor, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique, so two claimants of one role can both be real.
tips_feedback.why: Two Census Takers (Alice and Mallory) both censused Heidi. The Yakuza pushed the 'copying a dead player's will' line, but the town knew duplicate claims are legal, used Judy's Chronicler mark to test it, and hanged Heidi, who showed Informant.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name a corroborated mechanical break.
tips_feedback.why: Both hangs rested on mechanics: the census confirmed by Heidi's revealed role, and the gap between Erin's Fabricator visit and Mallory's death. That let me nominate Dave on a believable case and collect my second bounty.

tips_feedback.tip: Fire a Basic shot on a real lead by Day 2-3 rather than die holding tokens.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's N2 shot on Erin was good. His N3 Basic shot went at Niaj, a Village Oracle with Avenger, on thin suspicion. The Avenger killed Ivan, and the Serial Killer then won alone.

tips_feedback.tip: Read every cause of death: a Serial Killer death proves that killer is alive... hang them while the table is large.
tips_feedback.why: The town didn't follow this. It never went after the SK, even though SK kills on N1 and N2 proved one was alive and Frank's Medic claim could be checked against Dave's counts, so Frank won. That shows the tip is right.

tips_feedback.tip: Choose kills by what the victim could still find: Census Takers first.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza killed Alice, the Census Taker, on N1, but a second Census Taker (Mallory) had the same 3/3 result and posted it. Killing one investigator doesn't help when a role can repeat.

output.reason: Post-game reflection: reusable lessons and tip verdicts based on how this game went.

reasoning:
I'm drafting lessons from the bounty hunter role — noting that spending N1 on a target still secures the bounty even if another player also lands the kill, since claims count on co-kills too.

Looking at the tips feedback, I'm checking which guidance actually paid off: naming a corroborated mechanical break before voting Guilty helped land real hangs (Heidi, Dave), while role-claim awareness around dual Census Takers stopped town from falling for a fake "copier" line. The Vigilante's early shot on Erin was a good read, but the later shot on Niaj backfired badly since it hit a town Avenger — and the SK-hang-while-table-is-large advice never got followed, letting Frank slip through.

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.applies_to: Village investigators with a hard result (Census Taker, Sheriff, etc.)
lessons.tip: If a Fabricator could be in play, say publicly when you post a result: 'My will will never take this back. Any will that softens or retracts it is a Fabricator forgery.' Repeat the exact result in public chat, not only in your will. A forged 'I exaggerated, sorry' will is the Yakuza's best counter to a hard claim.

A census count of 0 Evil doesn't clear anyone as Good, because Neutrals are never counted. Bob was in my 0/3 group and was the Bounty Hunter. When you report a census, say which kind of player it can't rule out.

Once the Yakuza are confirmed by mechanics, switch to hunting the Neutral killer at once, while the table is still big. A Medic claim like 'I protected the victim but the SK's Strong attack got through' can't be checked. It is ideal Serial Killer cover, and so is 'I protected X N1' when X turned out to be Yakuza. Make unverified claimants explain their visits against the posted FT/visit counts.

Late in the game, don't shoot a claimed investigator just because their results can't be checked. Shooting into Village can trigger Avenger and lose two Village players in one night. Keep your token for the player whose claim actually conflicts with a death the game proved happened, such as an SK still alive.

After Night 1, centre your census on players who haven't claimed or who might be killers, not on players who already look trustworthy. The two random additions already spread the information, so aim the centre at the most useful unknown.

tips_feedback.tip: Post a result that bears on a vote in your first speech after getting it, with the night, target and exact wording.
tips_feedback.why: I posted my 3/3 census straight away on Day 2. Judy's Chronicler mark confirmed it, Heidi was hanged, and the town later hanged Dave even after my will was forged.

tips_feedback.tip: Only the Mayor, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique, so two claimants of one role can both be real.
tips_feedback.why: Frank and Ivan said outright that two Census Takers is legal. That beat the Yakuza line that I had copied Alice's will.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep your will current: past results, tonight's plan and what each outcome would mean.
tips_feedback.why: My accurate will was replaced by a Fabricator forgery. The tip doesn't warn that a will can be forged, and only the public record of my 3/3 claim kept the town on track.

tips_feedback.tip: Read every cause of death: a Serial Killer death proves that killer is alive. Keep a Neutral-killer suspect list and hang them while the table is large.
tips_feedback.why: The town ignored this after the Yakuza were wiped out. Frank's unverifiable Medic claim survived, and the SK won. Following the tip would have saved the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Fire a Basic shot on a real lead by Day 2-3 rather than die holding tokens.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's N2 shot on Erin killed a Yakuza and helped. His N3 shot on Niaj, the claimed Oracle, killed a Village player and set off Avenger, which killed Ivan. That handed the endgame to the SK.

output.reason: These are post-game lessons and tip verdicts drawn from how the census, the forged will and the SK endgame played out.

reasoning:
I should draft the lessons and tips. One key lesson: when a Census Taker gets a hard result, announce it publicly right away so a forged will can't contradict it later — stating openly that any conflicting will is proof of forgery. That public claim held up here since town still hanged Dave despite the forged will's excuse.

Other lessons: once the Yakuza were cleared, the real threat became the Serial Killer, and Frank's unverifiable medic claim about protecting a visitor was likely SK cover — town should pivot to hunting the neutral killer once the mafia faction is mostly confirmed. The Vigilante shooting a claimed Oracle on N3 caused damaging infighting that coordination could've avoided. A 0-evil Census result doesn't guarantee a Good group since Neutrals aren't counted (Bob being Neutral in that cleared trio proved this), and targeting unclaimed players would have been more useful than centering on Bob. Finally, Census Taker centering overlaps with Alice's own center, raising coordination questions about visit stacking.

Reviewing the tip feedback: posting a result relevant to a vote helped get Heidi hanged, keeping a will current partially backfired since mine got replaced by a Fabricator forgery (though Dave still hanged), and the Yakuza no-daytime-PM rule didn't prevent them from being caught through other mechanics. Reading every cause of death to build a neutral-killer suspect list would have helped avoid losing to the SK, two legitimate Census Taker claims coexisting was validated by Frank and Ivan's argument, and the Vigilante's early shot on Erin helped while the later N3 shot on Niaj backfired against Avenger.
