tips_feedback.tip: Read every cause of death: a Serial Killer... death proves that killer is alive... hang them while the table is large
tips_feedback.why: We knew a Serial Killer was alive from Night 1 but never hanged a suspect for it. Instead I wasted a night kill that couldn't have killed a Serial Killer anyway, so Frank won alone.

lessons.tip: Mark tomorrow's likeliest hang target, such as the centre of a census or the subject of a pending result. Then say publicly that the hang will reveal their role. That turns a disputed hang into a free test, and it gets wavering voters to vote Guilty. Spend your second mark on the next named suspect, so a Vigilante kill or a later hang also shows their role.

Distrust a dead accuser's will that softens or retracts their earlier public result if a known or suspected Fabricator visited them the night they died. A forged will usually 'admits' a lie and clears someone vaguely. Compare it with what the dead player said at trial, and with the wills of other investigators who back the original result.

Once the Yakuza look finished and a Serial Killer is still alive, don't shoot a claimed info role whose results fit the reveals. Aim at the claimant whose claim can't be checked and gives no feedback, like a Medic who 'protected' someone who died anyway or protected a revealed Yakuza. Shooting a Villager can also set off their Avenger trait and kill you, which hands the endgame to the killer.

After the last known Yakuza hangs, list every living player's claim and ask which one could hide the SK's nightly kill. Protector claims with no 'stopped an attack' result, and investigative claims with no checkable output, should top that list. Hang that player while you still outnumber the killer, and don't wait for another night.

Writing a mechanical conclusion in your will ('X revealed Yakuza, so the census is confirmed: hang Y and Z') keeps steering votes after you die. It also helps the town reject a forged will that contradicts it. Update your will every turn when the case changes.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name a corroborated mechanical break
tips_feedback.why: The Heidi hang rested on the census plus my Chronicler mark, which guaranteed a role reveal. The town voted 9-1 and the reveal showed Informant, confirming the census.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a mechanical result shows a player is Yakuza, those who defended them... are usually the next leads
tips_feedback.why: Erin and Dave both defended Heidi with the same 'Bounty Hunter copying' line. Both turned out to be Yakuza: Erin was shot by the Vigilante and showed Fabricator, and Dave was hanged.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens the first time they can change a vote ... Kill tokens need a break in the target's own claim
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's N2 shot on Erin followed the census and killed a Fabricator. His N3 shot broke the 'need a break' part: he shot the Oracle Niaj on suspicion, which killed a Villager, and Niaj's Avenger killed Ivan. That handed the game to the SK.

tips_feedback.tip: Read every cause of death ... Keep a Neutral-killer suspect list ... hang them while the table is large
tips_feedback.why: The town ignored this after the Yakuza were gone, and Frank's unverifiable Medic claim went untested. Frank was the SK and won alone. Following the tip would probably have caught him.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't hint at your role on Day 1 or 2
tips_feedback.why: I had to claim Chronicler on Day 2 so the mark could push the hang. The claim made me the SK's N2 target. It was still worth it, but claiming has a real cost for a claimant whose role is clearly useful.

lessons.applies_to: Village investigators with a hard result (Census Taker, Sheriff, etc.)
lessons.tip: If a Fabricator could be in play, say publicly when you post a result: 'My will will never take this back. Any will that softens or retracts it is a Fabricator forgery.' Repeat the exact result in public chat, not only in your will. A forged 'I exaggerated, sorry' will is the Yakuza's best counter to a hard claim.

A census count of 0 Evil doesn't clear anyone as Good, because Neutrals are never counted. Bob was in my 0/3 group and was the Bounty Hunter. When you report a census, say which kind of player it can't rule out.

Once the Yakuza are confirmed by mechanics, switch to hunting the Neutral killer at once, while the table is still big. A Medic claim like 'I protected the victim but the SK's Strong attack got through' can't be checked. It is ideal Serial Killer cover, and so is 'I protected X N1' when X turned out to be Yakuza. Make unverified claimants explain their visits against the posted FT/visit counts.

Late in the game, don't shoot a claimed investigator just because their results can't be checked. Shooting into Village can trigger Avenger and lose two Village players in one night. Keep your token for the player whose claim actually conflicts with a death the game proved happened, such as an SK still alive.

After Night 1, centre your census on players who haven't claimed or who might be killers, not on players who already look trustworthy. The two random additions already spread the information, so aim the centre at the most useful unknown.

tips_feedback.tip: Post a result that bears on a vote in your first speech after getting it, with the night, target and exact wording.
tips_feedback.why: I posted my 3/3 census straight away on Day 2. Judy's Chronicler mark confirmed it, Heidi was hanged, and the town later hanged Dave even after my will was forged.

tips_feedback.tip: Only the Mayor, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique, so two claimants of one role can both be real.
tips_feedback.why: Frank and Ivan said outright that two Census Takers is legal. That beat the Yakuza line that I had copied Alice's will.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep your will current: past results, tonight's plan and what each outcome would mean.
tips_feedback.why: My accurate will was replaced by a Fabricator forgery. The tip doesn't warn that a will can be forged, and only the public record of my 3/3 claim kept the town on track.

tips_feedback.tip: Read every cause of death: a Serial Killer death proves that killer is alive. Keep a Neutral-killer suspect list and hang them while the table is large.
tips_feedback.why: The town ignored this after the Yakuza were wiped out. Frank's unverifiable Medic claim survived, and the SK won. Following the tip would have saved the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Fire a Basic shot on a real lead by Day 2-3 rather than die holding tokens.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's N2 shot on Erin killed a Yakuza and helped. His N3 shot on Niaj, the claimed Oracle, killed a Village player and set off Avenger, which killed Ivan. That handed the endgame to the SK.

lessons.tip: Don't use guesses as wide random checks. Guess the role that would break the most important live claim, for example 'claimed Medic = Serial Killer' once an SK is known to be alive. A wrong guess only clears one role for one player, so spend each guess on the player you'd otherwise have to hang on a coin flip.

lessons.applies_to: Village players with the Avenger trait
lessons.tip: Once a Village Vigilante is alive and unclaimed late in the game, say publicly that you have Avenger. If the Vigilante shoots you, its hit-back kills a Village shooter, so a mistaken shot costs town two players. Saying it in public stops that shot. Only putting it in your will doesn't.

After a Fabricator flips, distrust the will of any player who died on a night the Fabricator visited them, especially a will that softens an earlier hard claim. Compare it with what that player said publicly while alive, and trust the public version.

Once the Yakuza are all gone and only an SK remains, town has to agree on a plan. Confirmed or claimed Village players commit to not shooting each other, the Vigilante holds or shoots the single SK suspect, and everyone claims fully. One misfire with 4 left hands the SK the game.

Count who must be the Neutral killer as players die. When the known SK is still alive and only a few unconfirmed players remain, push to hang the SK suspect while you still have the votes. Don't wait a night for more data, because the SK kills every night.

tips_feedback.tip: Post a result that bears on a vote in your first speech after getting it, with the night, target and exact wording.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory posted her 3/3 census on Day 2, and that led to Heidi's hang (she flipped Informant), Ivan's Vigilante kill on Erin and Dave's hang. It took apart all four Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens the first time they can change a vote... Kill tokens need a break in the target's own claim.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan shot Erin on N2 based on the census, which worked. On N3 he shot me, a Village Oracle, only because my results couldn't be checked. My Avenger hit-back then killed him, and the misfire gave the SK the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Read every cause of death: a Serial Killer death proves that killer is alive... hang them while the table is large.
tips_feedback.why: We correctly tracked that the SK was alive and narrowed it to Frank or Ivan. But we spent Day 3 hanging the last Yakuza and never got a Day to hang the SK, so the tip was right and we were too slow to act on it.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep your will current: past results, tonight's plan and what each outcome would mean.
tips_feedback.why: My will narrowed the SK to Frank or Ivan and explained the Avenger logic. Olivia then used it to identify Frank, though by then it was too late to win.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send teammates no daytime PMs.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza sent no PMs to each other and weren't exposed by PMs. They were caught only through mechanics: the census, the Chronicler marks and the Vigilante kill.

lessons.tip: Before you hang the last known Yakuza, plan that night publicly in the same Day. If the game keeps going after the hang, a Neutral killer is alive. List the living players who are left, get every one of them to hard-claim, and agree on the single target the Vigilante should shoot. Once that Day ends you can't plan any more, and the Neutral killer gets a free night.

lessons.applies_to: Saint and other no-action Village roles
lessons.tip: Once 5 or fewer players are alive and a Neutral killer is loose, claim your exact role, not just 'Village'. Players who only say 'Village' end up on the Vigilante's suspect list (Ivan's will named me as his top Serial Killer lead). A Saint gains little from hiding late, because the danger of being hanged is gone by then.

Avenger's hit-back is only Basic, so it can't get through the Standard Defense of a Serial Killer, Arsonist or Werewolf. It does kill a Vigilante or a Katana holder who has no Defense. Once the Yakuza are mostly gone, announce the trait publicly. A trigger-happy Vigilante will then think twice before shooting you, and you avoid losing two Village players in one night, as Niaj and Ivan did.

Be wary of a late Medic claim along the lines of 'I protected the player who died anyway, because the attack was Strong'. It can't be checked, and it fits a Serial Killer exactly, since Medic explains away visits and a missing result. Test it with visit counts, or put that claimant first in line when the game goes on after the Yakuza are gone.

In the endgame, shoot only on a mechanical break. Another Village claimant's Oracle misses or a quiet role claim are not breaks. Count who still needs to be ruled out as the Neutral killer, and shoot the claim that can't be checked (for example, an unconfirmed Medic) rather than the investigator whose claim fits.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name a corroborated mechanical break (census, Chronicler mark, etc.)
tips_feedback.why: Mallory's 3-of-3 census was backed by Judy's Chronicler mark. Heidi was revealed as Informant, and the town went on to wipe out the Yakuza within two Days.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a mechanical result shows a player is Yakuza, those who defended them... are the next leads
tips_feedback.why: Erin and Dave both defended Heidi using the same 'Bounty Hunter copying' line. Both turned out to be Yakuza: Erin was shot and Dave was hanged.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens... Kill tokens need a break in the target's own claim, votes or visits
tips_feedback.why: Ivan ignored this on Night 3 and shot Niaj, an Oracle whose claim held up, with no break. Niaj's Avenger killed Ivan, which handed the Serial Killer an easy 1-on-1. Following the tip would have saved the Village.

tips_feedback.tip: Read every cause of death: a Serial Killer death proves that killer is alive... hang them while the table is large
tips_feedback.why: It was correct, but the town ignored it. Serial Killer deaths on Night 1 and Night 2 showed one was alive, and Frank's Medic claim was never tested. Hunting the Serial Killer on Day 3 is what would have won the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Choose kills by what the victim could still find: Census Takers first
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza killed both Census Takers, but Mallory had already posted her result, which shows these kills only pay off before the result goes public.

summary: The Yakuza never recovered from Night 1. Frank (Serial Killer) killed Carol, the Yakuza Wiretap, which also killed Grace (Village Trapper) through their Bond. Two Census Takers (Alice and Mallory) both counted around Heidi and got 3/3 Evil for Heidi, Dave and Erin. The Yakuza killed Alice, but Mallory posted the result on Day 2. All three named Yakuza gave the same scripted defence ('a Bounty Hunter copied Alice's will'). Judy's Chronicler mark on Heidi made the hang a free test: Heidi showed Informant. On Night 2 Dave killed Mallory and Erin forged her will to say '2 of 3'. But Ivan's Vigilante shot killed Erin, Judy's second mark revealed her as Fabricator, and Erin's own will said 'N2: checking Mallory', which exposed the forgery. Dave was hanged on Day 3, which finished the Yakuza and gave Bob (Bounty Hunter) his second bounty. Four players remained: Frank (Serial Killer, falsely claiming Medic), Ivan (Vigilante), Niaj (Oracle) and Olivia (Saint). The game turned on Night 3. Ivan fired a Basic shot at Niaj, a Villager, on a weak lead. Frank also killed Niaj, and Niaj's Avenger trait then killed Ivan (Frank's Standard Defense stopped it). That left Frank and Olivia alone. Olivia couldn't hang Frank 1-vs-1, and Frank won on Night 4. Nobody pressed Frank's Medic claim, though by his own account he gave only free Standard protection to Judy after a Serial Killer was confirmed.

lessons.tip: Once the Yakuza are gone and the only enemy left is a Neutral killer with Standard Defense (Serial Killer, Arsonist, Werewolf), a Basic or Standard shot can't kill that killer. It can only kill Villagers. Hold your fire unless you can fire a Strong shot, and keep your vote alive for the Day hang.
lessons.evidence: Night 3: Ivan, with 2 tokens, shot Niaj with a Basic shot. If Frank had been his target, the shot would have bounced off. It killed a Village Oracle, and Niaj's Avenger killed Ivan back, leaving 1-vs-1 with the Serial Killer.

lessons.tip: Plan the endgame lock against a Neutral killer before the last Yakuza hang. With 4 left (3 Village and 1 Serial Killer), the Village must keep at least 2 voters alive into the 3-player Day. Any extra death from a Vigilante shot, a revenge trait or a hang turns it into a 2-player Day the Village can't win. Agree in public that nobody fires or acts riskily that night.
lessons.evidence: After Dave's hang the Village had Ivan, Niaj and Olivia against Frank. One death per night would have left Ivan and Olivia with 2 of 3 votes on Day 4. The extra Vigilante and Avenger deaths left Olivia alone, and her nomination of Frank failed 1-1.

lessons.tip: Check a protector's claim against the deaths. A Medic who says they used free Standard protection after a Serial Killer was confirmed, and 'lost' the target to a Strong attack, is giving a story nobody can check that also explains a Serial Killer kill. Make late claimants name tokens and protection levels, and rank them high on the Neutral-killer list.
lessons.evidence: Frank claimed Medic only on Day 3: 'N2 protected Judy (Standard), she died to the Serial Killer's Strong.' The Serial Killer had already killed Carol on N1. Nobody pressed him, and Ivan's will even called his claim consistent.

lessons.tip: When you forge a victim's will, keep your own will and public claims from naming that victim as your night target. If you die too, your will publicly links your visit to the forged will. Give a cover target that doesn't touch the forged victim.
lessons.evidence: Erin's will said 'N2: checking Mallory (result pending).' Niaj and Bob used it on Day 3 to explain Mallory's '2 of 3' will as a forgery, and Dave was hanged.

lessons.tip: Don't give every accused teammate the same defence line. When all the players named by one result use the same scripted rebuttal, it reads as coordinated and makes the result more believable. Vary the angles, or let one teammate concede.
lessons.evidence: Day 2: Dave, Erin and Heidi all argued 'a Bounty Hunter is copying Alice's will.' Ivan, Mallory, Niaj and Bob each cited that sameness as a reason to vote Guilty.

lessons.applies_to: Village (Chronicler and other reveal or test roles)
lessons.tip: Use a role-reveal mark on the player a hard claim names, and say so before the vote. The hang then tests the claim whichever way it goes, and wary voters can vote Guilty. Then mark the next player the result names.
lessons.evidence: Judy marked Heidi on N1 and announced it, and the town voted 9 Guilty, with Heidi the only Innocent. Heidi showed Informant. Judy then marked Erin, whose Fabricator reveal broke the forged-will plan.

lessons.tip: If you're named by a hard alignment result, don't spend teammates' PMs or kills on desperate saves. Dave's Day 3 PMs to Ivan and Frank were cited against him at once. Daytime PMs from a nominee only add evidence.
lessons.evidence: Ivan: 'Dave is also PMing for Innocent votes.' Dave was hanged 5-1.

lessons.tip: As a Serial Killer, claim a protective role late, once deaths can be fitted to it, vote with town on the confirmed Yakuza, and let the Village kill each other in the endgame. Target players who can still out you, or holders of revenge traits whose hit-back your Defense absorbs.
lessons.evidence: Frank voted Guilty on every Yakuza, claimed Medic only on Day 3, and survived both Avenger hit-backs with Standard Defense. He won alone.

tips_feedback.tip: Only the Mayor, Vulture, Hitman and Saint are Unique, so two claimants of one role can both be real... test both
tips_feedback.why: Mallory's census copied the target in Alice's will, and the Yakuza called it a 'copier'. The town didn't dismiss her, and Judy's mark tested the claim, confirming Heidi as Informant.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name a corroborated mechanical break
tips_feedback.why: Mallory's census was an uncorroborated claim, but Judy's mark made the Heidi hang a verifiable test. Voters cited that explicitly, and the reveal confirmed the census.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: send teammates no daytime PMs, and none at all on a Day a teammate is under pressure
tips_feedback.why: The tip held up. The Yakuza avoided PMs to each other on Day 2. On Day 3 Dave PMed Ivan and Frank for Innocent votes, and Ivan cited the PMs as a reason for Guilty.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep your will current: past results, tonight's plan and what each outcome would mean
tips_feedback.why: Erin, a Yakuza, followed it literally and wrote 'N2: checking Mallory' in her will. When she died the same night, that exposed her forgery of Mallory's will and sealed Dave's hang.

tips_feedback.tip: Fire a Basic shot on a real lead by Day 2-3 rather than die holding tokens
tips_feedback.why: It worked on N2: Erin was named by the census and died. On N3 Ivan fired a Basic shot at Niaj, a weak lead, when the only enemy left was a Serial Killer with Standard Defense. The shot could only ever kill a Villager, and Niaj's Avenger killed Ivan back, losing the Village its endgame majority.

tips_feedback.tip: Read every cause of death: a Serial Killer... death proves that killer is alive. Keep a Neutral-killer suspect list... and hang them while the table is large
tips_feedback.why: The tip was correct but ignored. The town knew a Serial Killer was alive from Night 1 and never built a suspect list. Frank's late Medic claim, with its free-Standard-only protection, went unexamined, and the Serial Killer won.

issues.description: At setup the harness logged '[ERROR tips_stale] tips/tips.md was last checked against an older version of the rules' and still gave that file to all 13 players. Players may have been working from advice that no longer matches the current rules (for example, rules on census reading or forged wills).

The Census Taker result says 'frames and disguises (the Katana holder, Notorious) don't change it'. Calling the Katana holder and Notorious 'disguises' mixes up terms: 'Disguised' is a separate trait that only affects exact-role checks. The wording could make a player think the Disguised trait matters to a census, or that Notorious is a kind of disguise. Better wording: 'appearance changes (Katana holder, framing, Notorious, Turncoat) don't affect it'.

Day 3: Ivan opened by saying 'Mallory's corrected census clears Dave of Yakuza'. He took her '2 of 3' will at face value, even though Erin had just been revealed as the Fabricator, the role that can forge the will of a player it visits who dies that night. Ivan's own shot had revealed her role to him. He had overlooked the forge mechanic. Niaj pointed it out, and Ivan then voted Guilty.
